strands.title: Social frameworks of remembering and language
strands.focus: Halbwachs’s memory inquiry and Meillet’s semantic history develop different objects from social relations. Shared vocabulary alone does not establish identical methods.
strands.works: Les Cadres sociaux de la mémoire (1925); “Comment les mots changent de sens” (1906)

rows.context: Social frameworks make remembering a relational process; later English selections are distinct from the original French works. The original French conclusion also addresses changes in traditions through relations between groups.
rows.works: Les cadres sociaux de la mémoire (1925); On Collective Memory, ed. and trans. Lewis Coser (1992 selections)

strands.title: Social frameworks of remembering
strands.focus: Family, religious and class contexts organize recollection; a collective framework is not proof of one identical group memory.
strands.works: Les cadres sociaux de la mémoire (1925); English selections (1992)

strands.title: Traditions in contact and conflict
strands.focus: Halbwachs explains revisions of collective remembering through contact with other groups and their traditions; social frameworks are not an assurance of a unanimous or unchanging past.
strands.works: Les cadres sociaux de la mémoire (1925), final concluding subsection

verification.note: Primary pp. 125–130 consulted in text; pp. 126 and 128 visually checked. Note 5 credits collaboration with Aleida Assmann; she is not co-author of this translation. The discussion engages Halbwachs, Warburg, oral-history research and, in note 8, Bourdieu’s 1972 Esquisse. Supports intersecting group memories and the communicative/cultural distinction as Assmann’s model, not a settled taxonomy. Original 1988 essay details appear in the opening footnote; cited books were not thereby read.
